To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
amphiphilic antibiotics are antifungal agents that can be designed to target fungal cells.

amphiphilic antibiotics derived from the classic drug kanamycin have antifungal activities that are comparable to those of the classic antibiotic amphotericin B, which is currently the most widely used antifungal.
4″ and 6″ di-aryl substitutions in kanamycin A derivatives result in compounds with antifungal activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new antifungal compounds and the understanding of the mechanisms of action.
the discovery of novel antifungals that are structurally different from the current antifungals in the clinic.
the development of new antifungals and the use of the cLogD parameter to predict the antifungal activity of amphiphilic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
amphiphilic antibiotics are a new class of antifungals.
amphiphilic antibiotics can have antifungal activity.
4″6″-di-aryl amphiphilically modified kanamycin antibiotics are antifungals and that the amphiphilicity of these antibiotics is a useful parameter to design the most membrane-active version.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
4″-aryl,6″-alkyl amphiphilicity is the best combination for antifungal activity.
the 4″,5″-disubstituted amphiphiles, including 4″,3″-disubstitution, are more active than the 4″-mono-substituted amphipiles against fungi.
amphiphilic antibiotics can be designed for antifungal activity by tuning the amphiphilicity parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
4″-substitution is a key factor for the antifungal activity of the amphiphilic derivatives of kanamycin.
amphiphilic antibiotics can be designed with the cLogD as a key parameter to optimize membrane-active antifungal properties.

amphiphilic 4″, 6″-substituted kanamycins have antifungal activities that are useful for the discovery of new antifungals and that the cLogD parameter can be used to design the most active amphiphilic versions of the compounds.
